claim: The overview example [1ix] I crawled towards the door is labelled “[direction: §4.4]”.
evidence_summary: The contents (p. 663) title §4.3 “Change of location: goal, source, path, and direction” and §4.4 “Metaphorical extension of the locative categories to other domains”. Direction of motion is treated in §4.3 under “Realisation of direction” (p. 688): “While to alone marks goal, towards marks direction”. §4.4 has direction only in static uses, as in [35i] The house faces towards the forest (p. 689).
finding: Change §4.4 to §4.3. Medium confidence: §4.4 does include direction examples, but only static ones, and [1ix] is literal motion. Ch. 4, p. 305, cites §4.4 for the way construction, which is also in §4.3 (CG-0171).
inference: Does the label point to the section that treats direction of motion?

evidence.establishes: The literal direction case is treated in §4.3.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
